name: Tymnes
bio: Tymnes is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 2nd century BC (?). Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 5 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 199, 211, 433, 477, 729).

poems.title: Book VII, 199: On an unknown bird called elaeus
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: Bird, nursling of the Graces, who didst modulate thy voice till it was like unto a halcyon’s, thou art gone, dear elaeus, and the silent ways of night possess thy gentleness and thy sweet breath.

poems.title: Book VII, 211
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: The stone tells that it contains here the white Maltese dog, Eumelus’ faithful guardian. They called him Bull while he still Jived, but now the silent paths of night possess his voice.

poems.title: Book VII, 433
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: His Spartan mother slew the Spartan Demetrius for transgressing the law. Bringing her sharp sword to the guard, she said, gnashing her teeth, like a Laconian woman as she was: “Perish, craven whelp, evil piece, to Hell with thee! He who is not worthy of Sparta is not my son.”

poems.title: Book VII, 477
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: Let not this, Philaenis, weigh on thy heart, that the earth in which it was thy fate to lie is not beside the Nile, but that thou art laid in this tomb at Eleutherna. From no matter where the road is the same to Hades.

poems.title: Book VII, 729
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: The omens were evil when fair Tritonis was brought to bed, for otherwise she would not have perished, unhappy girl, just after the child was born. With her this one babe brought down to Hades so much happiness, and it did not even live beyond the tenth dawn.

poems.title: Book XVI, 237: On the Same
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text: I behave like Priapus to everyone, even be he Cronos, so little distinction do I make between thieves here beside this kitchen-garden. Someone will tell me it is not meet for me to say this for the sake of greens and pumpkins. It is not meet, but I say it.

poems.title: On a Maltese Watch-Dog (Mackail)
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Here the stone says it holds the white dog from Melita, the most faithful guardian of Eumelus; Bull they called him while he was yet alive; but now his voice is prisoned in the silent pathways of night.

poems.title: The Silent Singing-Bird (Mackail)
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: O bird beloved of the Graces, O rivalling the halcyons in likeness of thy note, thou art snatched away, dear warbler, and thy ways and thy sweet breath are held in the silent paths of night.

poems.title: Far from Home (Mackail)
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Let not this be of too much moment to thee, O Philaenis, that thou hast not found thine allotted earth by the Nile, but this tomb holds thee in Eleutherne; for to comers from all places there is an equal way to Hades.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.199: ὄρνεον ὦ Χάρισιν μεμελημένον
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
ὄρνεον ὦ Χάρισιν μεμελημένον, ὦ παρόμοιον
ἀλκυόσιν τὸν σὸν φθόγγον ἰσωσάμενον,
ἡρπάσθης, φίλʼ ἐλαιέ· σὰ δʼ ἤθεα καὶ τὸ σὸν ἡδὺ
πνεῦμα σιωπηραὶ νυκτὸς ἔχουσιν ὁδοί.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.211: τῇδε τὸν ἐκ Μελίτης
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
τῇδε τὸν ἐκ Μελίτης ἀργὸν κύνα φησὶν ὁ πέτρος
ἴσχειν, Εὐμήλου πιστότατον φύλακα.
ταῦρόν μιν καλέεσκον, ὅτʼ ἦν ἔτι· νῦν δὲ τὸ κείνου
φθέγμα σιωπηραὶ νυκτὸς ἔχουσιν ὁδοί.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.433: τὸν παραβάντα νόμους Δαμάτριον
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
τὸν παραβάντα νόμους Δαμάτριον ἔκτανε μάτηρ
ἁ Λακεδαιμόνιον τὸν Λακεδαιμόνιον.
θηκτὸν δʼ ἐν προβολᾷ θεμένα ξίφος, εἶπεν, ὀδόντα
ὀξὺν ἐπιβρύκουσ’, οἷα Λάκαινα γυνά·
“ἔρρε κακὸν σκυλάκευμα, κακὰ μερίς, ἔρρε ποθʼ ᾅδαν
ἔρρε· τὸν οὐ Σπάρτας ἄξιον οὐδʼ ἔτεκον.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.477: μή σοι τοῦτο, Φιλαινί
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
μή σοι τοῦτο, Φιλαινί, λίην ἐπικάρδιον ἔστω,
εἰ μὴ πρὸς Νείλῳ γῆς μορίης ἔτυχες,
ἀλλὰ σ’ Ἐλευθέρνης ὅδʼ ἔχει τάφος· ἔστι γὰρ ἲση
πάντοθεν εἰς ἀίδην ἐρχομένοισιν ὁδός.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.729: εὐειδὴς Τριτωνὶς ἐπʼ οὐκ
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
εὐειδὴς Τριτωνὶς ἐπʼ οὐκ ἀγαθαῖς ἐλοχεύθη
κλῃδόσιν οὐ γὰρ ἂν ὧδʼ ὤλετο δαιμονίη
ἀρτιτόκος· τὰ δὲ πολλὰ κατήγαγεν ἓν βρέφος ᾅδην
σὺν κείνῃ· δεκάτην δʼ οὐχ ὑπερῆρεν ἕω.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.237: πάντα πριηπίζω, κἂν ᾖ
poems.author: Tymnes
poems.text:
πάντα πριηπίζω, κἂν ᾖ Κρόνος· οὐ διακρίνω
οὐδένα φῶρʼ οὕτω ταῖσδε παρὰ πρασιαῖς.
ἔπρεπε μὴ λαχάνων ἕνεκεν τάδε καὶ κολοκυνθῶν,
φήσει τις, με λέγειν. ἔπρεπεν ἀλλὰ λέγω.
